en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Eighth Chapter
The Discussion on Form in the Formless Realm: Is there form in the formless realms? Yes.

Is form-existence (rūpabhava) form-becoming (rūpagati), form-abode of beings (rūpasattāvāsa), form-saṃsāra (rūpasaṃsāra), form-maturation (rūpayoni), and the acquisition of the individuality of form (rūpattabhāvapaṭilābha)?
You should not say so... [and so forth] ...

Is it not the case that formless-existence (arūpabhava) is formless-becoming (arūpagati), formless-abode of beings (arūpasattāvāsa), formless-saṃsāra (arūpasaṃsāra), formless-maturation (arūpayoni), and the acquisition of the individuality of the formless (arūpattabhāvapaṭilābha)?
“Yes.
“If there is formless existence … and the acquisition of a formless body, then indeed, sir, you should not say:
‘There is form among the formless.’”
Is there matter in the formless realms? Yes.
Is five-aggregate existence a destiny, an abode of beings, saṃsāra, a matrix, a station of consciousness, or an acquisition of individuality?
It should not be said so...
[as before] ...Is it not the case that existence in the fourfold plane is the acquisition of a personal identity?
Yes, it is.
If four-aggregate existence is a destination … [and so on] … an acquisition of individuality, then surely you should not say:
"There is matter in the formless realms.
Is there matter in the realm of form? And is that form-existence, form-destination, form-abode of beings, form-saṃsāra, form-matrix, and acquisition of form-individuality?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is there matter among the formless realms, and is that a state of existence consisting of form, a destination of form, and so forth, up to the acquisition of a personal form consisting of matter?
You must not say so; ... [and so on] ...
Is there matter in the form realm, and is that a five-aggregate existence, a destination, ... [and so on] ... a acquisition of a personal identity? Yes.
Is there matter among the formless beings, and is that a five-aggregate existence, a destination, ... [and so on] ... a acquisition of a personal identity?

It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there matter in the formless realms, and is that formless existence, formless destiny, abode of formless beings, formless saṃsāra, formless womb, and acquisition of a formless selfhood? Yes.
Is there matter in the realm of form, and yet that is a formless existence, a formless destiny... [etc. ...a formless acquisition of individuality?
One should not say so... [etc.
...Is there matter among the formless beings, and yet that is a four-aggregate existence, a destiny... [etc. ...an acquisition of individuality?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is there matter in the form element, and is that fourfold existence, a destiny … [and so on] … an acquisition of a personal identity?
You must not say so … [and so on].
Is there matter in the formless realms? Yes.
But has it not been stated by the Blessed One that the formless is the escape from forms?
“Yes.
“If the Blessed One has stated that the escape from forms is the formless, then surely it should not be said:
‘There is form within the formless.’”
The Blessed One has stated that the escape from forms is the formless; yet is there form within the formless? Yes.

The Blessed One has stated that the escape from sensual desires is renunciation; yet is there sensual desire within renunciation? Is there taint within the taintless? Is there what is included within the unincluded?
It should not be said so... [etc.
...The discussion on form in the formless realm is finished.
